title: Q11
description:
“Your throne, O God, is forever and ever.”
Read: Psa 45 (whole psalm)
a) Psa 45 is a royal wedding song: a king is praised, armed for battle for truth and righteousness, and given a bride. What does that whole setting bring into Hebrews 1:8–9?
b) The king is called “God,” and yet “God, Your God, has anointed You.” What does Hebrews prove about the Son by holding both lines together, instead of choosing one?
